transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what brought you in to see me?

Hi, thank you. Well, I came in because I just can't seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. I'm a loan officer, and lately I'll just stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list and reread the same line over and over again. And then I end up putting off making my calls, because... I don't know, even simple decisions just feel a lot harder than they should right now.
How long have you been experiencing this trouble concentrating and making decisions?
Well, it's been a while. I'd say this has really been going on since my close friend died... which was a little over two years ago now.
Over these past two years, would you say you've felt sad or down nearly every day, most of the day, or has your mood come and gone in more distinct episodes?

I'd say it's been nearly every day. It doesn't really come and go in episodes. Most days, there's just this... dull heaviness sitting with me. Even when I'm at the community center, or out in my garden—places that really used to lift me up—I feel like I'm just going through the motions. I'm there, and I have a smile pasted on, but that heavy feeling is pretty much with me most of the day.
During these past two years, has there ever been a period of two months or longer when you felt back to your normal self, without that heavy, down feeling?

No, not really. I don't think there's been a time like that. It's just been... pretty constant since she passed. I can't remember a stretch of even a few weeks, let alone two months, where I felt like my old self again.
Over these past two years, have you noticed significant changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. My sleep is... well, it's pretty much the same as it's always been. I don't have trouble falling asleep, and I'm not sleeping the day away or anything. It's just my normal routine, really.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight, either an increase or decrease?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, my weight has stayed pretty much exactly the same. I still eat my regular meals... so, no real changes with my appetite either. It's just been normal.
Over these past two years, have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy most days?

Yes, actually, I have. I wake up tired... even after a full night of sleep. And it really doesn't take much to wear me out. By the time I’ve done a couple of client calls for work, or just gone out to water the tomatoes, my body feels like I’ve put in a whole day already. The energy just isn't there.
Over these past two years, have you noticed feeling low self-esteem, or being unusually critical of yourself?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I know I'm tired a lot, but I don't really beat myself up over it or feel bad about who I am. I just... do my work, do my best with the clients, and that's that. So, no, my self-esteem seems fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic, non-episodic depressed mood present nearly every day for over two years following the death of a close friend, with no period of remission lasting two months or more. Associated symptoms include anhedonia, low energy/fatigue, and impaired concentration/indecisiveness—meeting the minimum two additional symptoms required for Persistent Depressive Disorder. Sleep, appetite, and self-esteem are unaffected, and there is no evidence of a discrete major depressive episode with full symptom criteria or of manic/hypomanic episodes. The chronicity (>2 years), sub-threshold but persistent symptom pattern, and lack of episodic mood elevation support F34.1 (Dysthymia) over recurrent MDD or adjustment disorder.
